openings.claim: A behind-desk reader-to-position register, with numbered shelf regions, could remove household-surname ambiguity from retrieval while retaining clerk-only identity checks.
openings.delta: Storage addresses depend on physical position rather than surname. This replaces surname-based search; it does not merely refine divider spacing.
openings.prediction: Address lookup reduces retrieval time particularly for household-name mismatches, including books whose recorded location was already correct.
openings.rival_prediction: Updating the existing exception slip at each move is the nearest alternative: it improves stale-location cases, but correctly recorded household-name mismatches remain slow.
openings.defeat: Correct address lookup remains slow, or mismatched surnames show no greater search burden than matched surnames.
openings.probe: Use existing paper and cards for a small shadow lookup comparison without changing handoffs or moving books. Record surname mismatch, location accuracy and lookup time. Cap all daily preparation, including this probe, at ten clerk-minutes; omit the probe if no time remains.
assumptions: Fit evaluates the capped shadow probe; operational replacement and the 95% target remain unproven.
Reliable reader-to-hold identification and affordable register maintenance require confirmation.

openings.claim: Keeping newly arrived holds on the cart through the evening window may make retrieval faster by preventing location churn.
openings.delta: The cart becomes the deliberate arrival location for that window instead of an exception awaiting shelving.
openings.prediction: With comparable arrival volume and book size, a fixed cart batch retains fast retrieval and generates fewer second-location searches.
openings.rival_prediction: Immediate shelving with accurate move updates is the nearest alternative: it performs equally well if small cart volume, rather than location stability, explains O4.
openings.defeat: Comparable batches become slower on the stationary cart, or books cannot fit without obstructing existing cart use.
openings.probe: Trial a small already-arrived batch only after confirming cart capacity and required return use. Keep labels behind the desk, retain clerk identification, measure complete pickup time and wrong-reader handoffs, and enforce the ten-minute total preparation ceiling.
assumptions: Cart capacity and competing return demands are unknown.
The synthetic ten-pickup sample establishes neither scalability nor a tested benefit.
